Memory summary

The final implementation used one cooperative CUDA megakernel launch per decode step to fuse the four-layer KDA/KDA/KDA/MLA block and its MoE stages. Relevant prior context

The run began with an H100 80 GB device even though the task specified an RTX PRO 6000. The first megakernel was correct but slower than baseline (peak_fraction: 0.5055). Profiling exposed long scalar GEMV reductions, low occupancy, and synchronization overhead. A microtest also found that __shared__ memory is block-private: grid-strided staging had left each block with only part of the input vector.

The successful tuning direction was to parallelize each GEMV reduction across 32 lanes and reduce with warp shuffles. The agent reported that this cut an individual GEMV from roughly 290 µs to 33 µs. Fusing KDA q/k/v/g projections, routed-expert gate/up and down work, and residual epilogues reduced the kernel from about 169 stages to roughly 60. Four-way output chunking, 64-lane groups, K-loop unrolling, streaming loads, and smaller cooperative grids were slower or infeasible; the final configuration restored 32-lane helpers and a 256-block grid without a launch-bounds cap.

Important non-obvious context

The task’s peak_fraction is baseline latency divided by solution latency, geometrically averaged: it is a speedup multiple, not a fraction of hardware peak. The prompt and problem.yaml specify an RTX PRO 6000, but the benchmark labels the GPU H100 and the probe reported an NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3.
